packs.name: HexStrike-inspired workflow and payload pack
packs.license_note: Reimplemented locally from high-level ideas only.
packs.summary: Workflow-oriented pack for choosing the next single Burp change, ordering variant requests, and recognizing when two findings belong to the same escalation chain.

workflow_focus: Keep one best-next-step, one backup step, and one stop condition visible to the operator at all times.
Join two findings only when the same request, same object boundary, or same workflow transition ties them together.
payload_strategy: Order variants from lowest-noise confirmation to highest business-signal confirmation.
Prefer payload ladders that explain what to compare after each send, not only what to send.
reporting_focus: Keep variant naming stable so the strongest delta can be moved directly into the report as a proof artifact.
Record why one variant was better than the others, not just that it worked.

workflow_focus: Model the flow as pre-login, login, post-login, logout, and stale-session replay before trying extra branches.
If another scanner-marked issue exists on the same auth flow, use it as a chained branch only when the same session boundary explains both.
payload_strategy: Order the ladder as missing token, stale token, lower-privilege token, then post-logout replay.
After each send, compare redirect chain, cookie rotation, and protected-path visibility.

workflow_focus: Keep the route and object fixed while toggling only one server-managed field at a time.
Prefer fields that map directly to role, ownership, approval, or billing state.
payload_strategy: Start with low-risk role or status fields before broader nested-object mutations.
Compare silent acceptance, reflected acceptance, and state-change acceptance separately.
Sequence SSRF checks as absolute URL, alternate scheme, relative path, and normalization edge case.
Compare parser acceptance before assuming outbound network behavior.
Sequence the CSRF comparison as baseline token, token removed, then origin or referer mismatch.
Keep the route and state-change target fixed while comparing token and browser trust signals.

workflow_focus: Treat storage, render, and viewer privilege as three separate workflow checkpoints.
Escalate only after the render survives beyond the submitting request context.
payload_strategy: Sequence the checks as harmless context probe, storage confirmation, render confirmation, then viewer-impact confirmation.
Keep the viewer path explicit in tab naming and evidence notes.

workflow_focus: Treat mass-assignment as a state-change workflow first, not only an input-validation issue.
Confirm which state-change field moved and whether the move persists on a follow-up read.
Treat desynchronization as the first workflow checkpoint before any downstream branch such as queue poisoning or access-control impact.
